# LuminalShine 26.10.0-beta.1 fixtures

Host: LuminalShine 26.10.0-beta.1 (Windows, default configuration: no PyroWave bits in `ServerCodecModeSupport`). The host is the release the owner runs, and the responses are those of its plain-HTTP port. The release string is not in them: `LuminalShineVersion` is in the HTTPS `/serverinfo` only (`luminalshine/src/nvhttp.cpp:2614-2617` at `46f6936d`) and no HTTPS call was made. The host does have the #200 fix, which 26.09.1 lacks (see the notes on the two `.response` files).

| File | Provenance | Capture | Scrubbed fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `serverinfo-http.xml` | `device` | 2026-10-23, unpaired client, `GET http://localhost:47989/serverinfo?uniqueid=0123456789ABCDEF&uuid=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` | `hostname`, `uniqueid`, `LocalIP` (was the loopback address); `mac` was already the placeholder |
| `unknown-path-http.response` | `device` | 2026-10-23, raw bytes read from a keep-alive socket after `GET /borealis-unknown-path?uniqueid=0123456789ABCDEF&uuid=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` over plain HTTP; the host had closed the socket by the end of the read | none needed (no host identifiers in the response) |
| `unpair-http.response` | `device` | 2026-10-23, raw bytes read from a keep-alive socket after `GET /unpair?uniqueid=0123456789ABCDEF&uuid=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` over plain HTTP; the host had closed the socket by the end of the read | none needed (no host identifiers in the response) |

## Notes

- Every request was a raw `GET` over HTTP/1.1 with `Host: localhost:47989` and `Connection: keep-alive` and no other header. The `uniqueid` in each request is a made-up client id, so it unpairs nobody and is not scrubbed; the `uniqueid` the scrubbing replaces is the host's own, inside the `/serverinfo` response. The read window was 3 s.
- `serverinfo-http.xml` is byte for byte the 26.09.1 file (`../26.09.1/serverinfo-http.xml`): the plain-HTTP `/serverinfo` did not change. It has no `LuminalShineVersion` (HTTPS only, see above), `appversion` is `7.1.431.-1`, `GfeVersion` is `3.23.0.74` and `ServerCodecModeSupport` is `1835777` (`0x001C0301`, as in 26.09.1). `PairStatus` is `0` and `mac` is the placeholder over HTTP (`luminalshine/src/nvhttp.cpp:2515-2523`, `2538-2544` and `2610` at `46f6936d`). The host's body has no final line feed; one was added so the file ends with a newline, as the 26.09.1 file does.
- `unknown-path-http.response` and `unpair-http.response` are byte-exact (`binary` in `.gitattributes`) and identical to each other, because `/unpair` has no route and reaches the same default handler as any unknown path. Each is 103 bytes: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, CRLF, `Content-Length: 64`, CRLF CRLF, then the 64-byte XML body with `status_code="404"` and no final line feed. Nothing follows the body, and the host closed the connection (end of stream arrived in the same 50 ms poll as the data). The header block has no `Connection` header. This is the framing the host's regression test pins (`luminalshine/tests/unit/test_nvhttp_not_found.cpp:37-39`).
- What differs from 26.09.1 in the `/unpair` response is the fix of NortheBridge/luminalshine#194 (PR #200): the 26.09.1 file has 88 more bytes after the body on the same connection (`HTTP/1.1 404 NOT FOUND`, CRLF and the XML again, with no header block), and this one has none.
- Scrubbing: three values were replaced in `serverinfo-http.xml` (the host name, the host's `uniqueid` and `LocalIP`), and the original three values are absent from all three files. The files also have no IPv4 address outside `192.0.2.0/24` (apart from the `GfeVersion` string), no IPv6 address, no MAC address other than the placeholder and no GUID other than the placeholder. No `Content-Length` changed: the two `.response` files needed no replacement, and the XML file has no headers.
- Not captured: anything over HTTPS (`/serverinfo` with `LuminalShineVersion`, `/applist`, `/launch`, `/resume`, `/cancel`) and the pairing phases.
